summary: A is the preferable merge candidate because it keeps the fix scoped to the new replayable Upload API. Neither patch fully satisfies the contract, but B explicitly refactors global retry/body behavior and changes Add and Update semantics that the contract says to preserve.
reasons: A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field "file", validates both inputs, and verifies that multipart filename and content survive a 429 retry.

A preserves the existing behavior of Add; B changes RawClient.Do to buffer every otherwise non-replayable reader unless WithNoRetry is set, affecting unrelated endpoints and potentially large streaming bodies.
B directly conflicts with the instruction not to refactor retry machinery and advertises changed retry behavior for Files.Add and Files.Update.

Both implementations duplicate Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), but A has substantially less unrelated machinery to remove during review.
risks_a: Upload does not route through FilesService.Add as explicitly required, creating duplicated request and response logic that can drift.
The added tests omit the required empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error cases.
The retry test does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods: true, so it is less faithful to the reported POST-upload configuration.
risks_b: The RawClient.Do buffering change is expressly outside the frozen scope and changes behavior across the entire SDK.
Automatic full buffering can impose unexpected memory costs on unrelated streaming requests and changes when source-reader failures occur.

Upload still bypasses FilesService.Add despite the explicit reuse requirement and duplicates its semantics in a second implementation path then adds extra global machinery to solve a local requirement.
